title: 2018 AMC 12B Problem 12
statement: Side \(\overline{AB}\) of \(\triangle ABC\) has length \(10.\) The bisector of angle \(A\) meets \(\overline{BC}\) at \(D,\) and \(CD=3.\) The set of all possible values of \(AC\) is an open interval \((m, n).\) What is \(m+n?\)

solutions.text:
Let \(q=AC\) and \(r=BD.\) The angle bisector theorem gives \(\tfrac{q}{3}=\tfrac{10}{r},\) so \(r=\tfrac{30}{q}.\)

Applying the triangle inequalities to sides \(q,\) \(10,\) and \(3+r\) and substituting \(r=\tfrac{30}{q}\) yields \((q-15)(q+2)\lt0\) and \((q-3)(q+10)\gt0\) (the third inequality holds automatically). Together these force \(3\lt q\lt15.\)

So \((m,n)=(3,15)\) and \(m+n=18.\)

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(AC=q,\) so \(BD=\dfrac{30}{q};\) then apply the three triangle inequalities
